description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Governance for Solutions works through local coalitions of stakeholders in government, private sector, and civil society to identify governance bottlenecks that inhibit effective delivery of public services, efficient use of public resources, and the protection of public goods such as natural resources. The activity will help identify groups or institutions that are effectively addressing these challenges; learn from these experiences; devise interventions that build on success; and adapt programming for further improvement. GfS will identify issues based on the USAID/Malawi's CDCS and the viability of coalitions in effecting change. Health, education, agriculture, and natural resources management are key GfS sectors, with human resource and financial management as cross-cutting challenges. Illustrative issues include teacher performance, drug theft, and more efficient agricultural subsidies that have direct and attributable impacts on aid effectiveness and the Mission's development objectives..GfS contributes to the Malawi ICS's Goal 1: Democratic and Accountable Governance; and Objective 1.2 Public service providers improve the integrity and quality of public services, particularly those supported with U.S. foreign assistance. It also supports CDCS (2020 - 2025) Development Objective 1, which seeks to improve public sector effectiveness and accountability at the national and decentralized levels. The activity also prioritizes the cross-cutting goals of gender equity and youth engagement....
